meta.parties: Leo Et Al. v. The Land Commissioner

rules.statement: An inferior tribunal making a judicial decision must prove the existence of an essential condition precedent to its jurisdiction, and if that condition is not objectively satisfied, the tribunal has acted in excess of jurisdiction.
rules.supporting_quote: "No tribunal of limited jurisdiction can give itself jurisdiction by a wrong decision on a point collateral to the merits of the case upon which the limits to its jurisdiction depends." Banbury v. Fuller [(1853) 9 Ex. D. 29 at 35.]
